title: OSS weights assembly pipeline: deterministic conversion, safety assertions, and performance profile publish
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an end-to-end onboarding pipeline that takes community/OSS weight uploads through deterministic conversion, safety & license assertions, functional smoke tests, and automated performance profiling. The goal is a single, auditable workflow that outputs a pinned model artifact (canonical pin), a runtime-compatible bundle, and a published performance profile to the model catalog. This ticket focuses on the core assembly job, gating criteria, and the automated publish steps.
acceptance_criteria: Given an OSS weights tarball + manifest, the pipeline performs checksum and signature validation and produces a deterministic converted bundle reproducible across two independent runs
The pipeline runs a license scan + basic safety heuristics (weight anomaly detector) and flags any issues to a human review queue
A standardized smoke test suite (generation, max-seq stability, KV cache reuse) completes within defined thresholds for latency and memory on the selected profiling hardware

A performance profile (P95 latency, tokens/s throughput, peak GPU memory, recommended batching & quantization profile) is published to the model catalog as a new versioned profile linked to the canonical pin
If any gate fails we prevent publish and create a tracked review issue with links to artifacts and logs
technical_notes: Conversion step uses the new 'conv-runner' k8s Job with immutable input/output S3 prefixes to enable reproducibility and garbage-collection policies
We will favor deterministic ops: stable random seeds, fixed exporter versions, and checksum-based caching for conversion artifacts
Quantization candidates are generated in a separate parallel job (4-bit q8_0 / 3-bit checks) limited to a curated set of kernels to avoid unsupported execution paths
Profiling harness will run on a dedicated perf node type (A100-40GB / H100-80GB) depending on model footprint; hardware mapping rules live in infra-config repo

We intentionally keep safety heuristics minimal at pipeline level (license check, large-sparse-matrix anomalies, embedding drift smoke) and route content safety to the Review Queue handled by Security team
Publish semantics: create canonical_pin, attach runtime bundle (digest), and upload performance profile JSON to /catalog/profiles/<pin>/v1.json with stable schema and changelog entry
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): run pipeline only on internal curated OSS inputs (10 models), manual approvals required before publish
Phase 2 (beta): enable automatic publish for low-risk licenses (Apache/MIT) and models <20B params; human review required for permissive/unknown licenses
Phase 3 (ga): open pipeline to community submissions with rate limits and quota; integrate with intake web UI and submitter notifications
Canary policy: new conversion image rolled out to 5% of conversions and monitored for divergence in deterministic outputs for 48 hours before full rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for conv-runner CLI and manifest parser (CI)
Integration tests: feed known seed tarballs and assert identical bundle digests across two runs
Smoke suite: generation correctness on canonical prompt set, KV cache warm/hit rate checks, catastrophic OOM detection
Performance regression tests: compare latency/throughput to baseline profiles and fail on >15% regression
E2E dry-run: pipeline run with publish disabled that exercises all gates and produces full logs/artifacts
telemetry_requirements: Emit conversion job metrics: duration_ms, bytes_in, bytes_out, exit_code
Profiling metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens_per_second, peak_gpu_memory_mb, flop_estimate
Gate metrics: gate_passed:bool per gate (checksum, license, smoke), and human_review_count
User-facing catalog metadata: pin_created_at, profile_version, supported_hw_labels
security_considerations: Run conversions inside a restricted k8s namespace with no egress to limit exfiltration risk
Scan uploaded manifests for suspicious URLs or execution hooks and quarantine if found
KMS-backed signing of canonical pins and signed metadata blobs to ensure provenance
Require Security team approval for publish when license is unknown or when model contains flagged tokens from the safety heuristic
implementation_steps: 1) Define input manifest schema and mandatory fields (weight_checksum, architecture, tokenizer_info, license)
2) Implement conv-runner k8s job and image with deterministic exporter toolchain
3) Add license-checker lambda and integrate into pipeline gating
4) Wire the profiling harness to perf nodes and implement result aggregation
5) Implement publish step: canonical pin creation, artifact storage, and profile upload
6) Hook up human review queue (Linear auto-issue creation) and Slack notify channel
7) Add CI integration tests and deploy conv-runner image behind feature flag
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-deterministic conversions due to floating point variance across hardware. Mitigation: pin exporter versions, use deterministic ops and run cross-hardware checks; if variance persists, add 'variance-tolerance' threshold and post-fix conversion artifacts

Risk: Slow profiling increases cost. Mitigation: sample small representative sequences and limit profiling to 3 configurations (default, small-batch, quantized) and reuse cached results when model identical digest found
Risk: License ambiguity blocks throughput. Mitigation: automated license heuristics + fallback human review with SLAs; maintain whitelist/blacklist for rapid decisions
Risk: Security/supply-chain vector from community weights. Mitigation: run conversions in isolated runtime, restrict egress, sign artifacts, and preserve raw uploads for audit
